result.title: MEMIG: Self-evolving Memory Construction for Antibody Optimization
result.summary: Memory has become central to self-evolving LLM agents, which store and retrieve experience from past rollouts to guide future decisions. Existing systems represent this experience as free-form natural language and maintain it by rewriting, which fits tasks whose experience is narratable. However, in scientific discovery and optimization, experience is often a quantity measured by an oracle under a specific context. Rewriting it as text leaves no index for where a record should be, replaces a measurement with a description, and cannot express how interventions interact. To address this, we argue that agent memory for biomolecule optimization should instead be indexable, quantitative, and structured, and we introduce MEMIG. This memory construction framework realizes these three properties. In detail, MEMIG addresses each insight with a domain-grounded identifier and accumulates the quantitative effect measured by a property oracle, so that updates remain local and retrieval becomes an exact lookup. Next, MEMIG connects insights whose interventions are applied together and measures their epistasis by decomposing each evaluated set. Our results show that MEMIG improves performance in most settings across in silico antibody optimization tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 MEMIG，一种面向抗体优化的自进化智能体记忆构建框架：用领域标识符索引经验条目、累积属性预测器测得的定量效应，并通过分解评估集合测量共同干预间的上位效应，以替代自由文本重写式记忆。
AI.relevance_reason: 非视觉、非推理期 latent 生成工作，但其「可索引、定量、结构化」记忆与精确查表检索，或许可为 LVR 中证据缓存结构、跨干预的贡献分配提供问题表述上的启发，可供核查。
